def: A drug that kills or expels parasitic worms (helminths). Examples are albendazole, mebendazole, ivermectin and praziquantel.
The nematode Trichuris trichiura, acquired by swallowing eggs from contaminated soil. It lives in the cecum and colon and can cause bloody diarrhea and rectal prolapse in heavy infection.
A substance that increases salivary flow, such as pilocarpine or cevimeline. Used to treat dry mouth in Sjogren syndrome.
The vaginal opening (entrance to the vagina).
Sharp chest wall pain with breathing from muscle inflammation, classically caused by coxsackie B virus (Bornholm disease).
Small, non-enveloped, positive-sense RNA viruses that include norovirus, a common cause of acute gastroenteritis outbreaks.
Non-enveloped virus with a double-stranded segmented RNA genome. Rotavirus is a member and causes infant diarrhea.
A narrow, unused colon seen in newborns with distal bowel obstruction, as in meconium ileus or intestinal atresia.
A collection of fluid between the layers of the tunica vaginalis around the testis. Painless and transilluminates.
Sitting upright and leaning forward with arms propped, to keep the airway open. A sign of epiglottitis or severe respiratory distress.
Located outside the chest; an extrathoracic airway obstruction (such as in the neck) mainly impairs inspiration.
The period before the onset of labor during pregnancy.
Excessive, diffuse hair shedding. Telogen effluvium occurs a few months after stress, illness or childbirth.
Describing cells with few or no granules. The hypogranular variant of acute promyelocytic leukemia has promyelocytes with few granules.
Maternal antibody formation against a fetal red cell antigen, such as Rh D, causing hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn.
Cationic polypeptide antibiotics that disrupt bacterial membranes (polymyxin B and colistin). Active against gram-negative bacteria and cause nephrotoxicity.
Warty genital growth caused by HPV types 6 and 11. Called a genital wart.
Squamous cells with a wrinkled nucleus and clear perinuclear halo, the cytologic sign of HPV infection.
The flagellated, blood-stage form of Trypanosoma that infects humans. T. cruzi (Chagas disease) and T. brucei (sleeping sickness) occur in this form.
Tending to cause vomiting, as with high-risk chemotherapy such as cisplatin.
High serum magnesium, often from renal failure or magnesium infusion. Causes loss of deep tendon reflexes, hypotension and respiratory depression.
A substance that stimulates cell division, such as growth factors.
Relating to the pituitary gland (hypophysis), as in the hypophyseal portal system.
Tending to raise blood glucose or cause diabetes. Growth hormone, cortisol and glucagon are diabetogenic.
A vasopressin V1a/V2 receptor antagonist given IV for hyponatremia from SIADH. Blocks water reabsorption in the collecting duct.
Intermediate in steroid hormone synthesis, made from pregnenolone by 17-alpha-hydroxylase; leads to DHEA and 17-hydroxyprogesterone.
Caused by an inherited defect in hormone synthesis, as in dyshormonogenetic goiter from thyroid enzyme defects.
Gene expression that depends on parent of origin, with one allele silenced by methylation. Explains Prader-Willi and Angelman syndromes.
Delicate connective tissue surrounding individual nerve fibers within a fascicle.
Deposition of pink, glassy, homogeneous protein material in tissue, as in arteriolosclerosis.
Staining with acidic dyes such as eosin (pink-red). Acidophilic cytoplasm indicates abundant protein or damaged cells.
Low urinary calcium excretion, as seen with thiazide diuretics or Gitelman syndrome.
A DPP-4 inhibitor for type 2 diabetes that raises incretin levels, increasing glucose-dependent insulin release.
Conversion of androgens to estrogens by the enzyme aromatase, in fat tissue and the ovary. Testosterone becomes estradiol.
Thickening of the stratum granulosum of the skin, seen in lichen planus.
Immature, malignant skeletal muscle cells seen in rhabdomyosarcoma, often with cross-striations.
Orientation of the two DNA strands running in opposite 5' to 3' directions.
Covalent bond linking the 3' hydroxyl of one nucleotide to the 5' phosphate of the next, forming the DNA or RNA backbone.
A point mutation substituting a purine for a pyrimidine or the reverse. Contrasts with transition.
DNA sequences that bind repressor proteins and reduce transcription of nearby genes.
